sources.entry: Flipic - Photo culling viewer: arrow-key paging through a folder, 100% focus check, XMP ratings that Lightroom and Capture One read, on-device cleanup mode. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/xmasdong/flipic) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Flipic is a macOS photo viewer for culling shoots: open a folder, page through with arrow keys, rate and flag photos, and write star ratings as XMP that Lightroom and Capture One can read.
summary.what_it_does: Flipic opens a photo's folder directly without importing or creating a library, and lets you page through images with the arrow keys, keeping prefetched neighbours ready in the background. You can zoom to 100% at the mouse position to check focus, compare photos side by side, and rate with 1 to 5 stars. Ratings are written as XMP: into the file for JPEG and HEIC, or into a same-named .xmp sidecar for camera RAW. Flagged photos get a Finder tag named Flipic. A culling mode, which runs locally with Apple's Vision framework, groups similar bursts, duplicates, closed eyes and blurry shots and suggests which to keep. The app also includes batch format conversion, batch rename, rotation, slideshow, export, and handoff to external editors such as Lightroom or Photoshop. The README says the app works offline with no account, and that the viewing and culling features are free.
use_cases: cull a photo shoot after importing from a memory card
check focus at 100% before deciding which burst frame to keep
rate and flag photos before opening them in Lightroom or Capture One
clean up hundreds of event photos with duplicate and blur detection
view RAW and JPEG folders without making an import catalog
batch convert or rename a folder of photos
how_to_run: Download Flipic.dmg from the project site or GitHub Releases and drag Flipic into Applications
git clone the repository and cd into flipic
For Xcode: install XcodeGen, then run xcodegen generate
notable: Writes star ratings as XMP, readable by Lightroom, Bridge and Capture One, with RAW ratings in sidecar files so RAW data is untouched
Never imports photos: no copies, no catalog, nothing left behind when closed
Culling mode runs on-device with the macOS Vision framework and only groups and recommends; deletion is always a user action and undoable
Pages through large folders by decoding at screen size and prefetching neighbours, with cache limits set by RAM
Companion files like RAW+JPG pairs and Live Photo MOVs move, delete and copy together
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or newer; JPEG XL needs macOS 14 and HDR display needs macOS 14 and a compatible screen

The README describes a paid Flipic Pro tier (one-time ¥68, 7-day trial in the download) with extra features; the code for Pro is not in the public repository, and builds from source are the free version
Culling detections can be wrong, so the README advises reviewing before deleting
Interface is in Chinese and English in the README, with 14 languages mentioned in the app
